note: Placeholders like ${VAR} are filled in by mcp-gen from .env.local or the environment. ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} is the project folder.

servers.name: MCPVault (Obsidian vault access)
servers.what: Lets Alterbrain read, search and write notes in your Obsidian vault.
servers.notes: Works on the vault folder directly, so Obsidian does not need to be open. Writes only inside the vault. The vault path uses the project folder placeholder; mcp-gen should turn it into an absolute path if the client does not expand it [Unverified]. Last push 2026-10-02.

servers.name: MCPVault (read-only)
servers.what: The same vault access, but it can only read and search. Nothing can be changed.
servers.notes: Use this instead of mcpvault for quarantined or cloud jobs, or if you want a vault that cannot be edited. Do not enable both at once.

servers.name: Playwright (Microsoft)
servers.what: Lets Alterbrain open web pages, read them and fill in forms in a browser.
servers.notes: Clicking submit-like buttons is held back by the outbound guard unless you allow web-forms. Pre-1.0 version, so pinned exactly. Never log in to sensitive accounts through it. Last push 2026-09-28.

servers.name: MarkItDown (Microsoft)
servers.what: Turns PDFs, Word, PowerPoint and Excel files into plain text Alterbrain can read.
servers.notes: Needs uv installed. The package is still an alpha release, so it is pinned exactly. Meant for local use only: never expose it to a network. Reads files only.

servers.name: Fetch (Model Context Protocol)
servers.what: Downloads a web page and gives Alterbrain its text.
servers.notes: This one is a Python package, so it runs through uvx, not npx. Reads only. The page text is treated as untrusted data.

servers.name: Filesystem (Model Context Protocol)
servers.what: Lets Alterbrain read and write files, limited to the folders you allow.
servers.notes: Only the vault folder is allowed by default. Add other folders only if you are sure. The npm licence field points to the repo file, which mixes MIT and Apache-2.0 during a relicensing, so check before redistributing.

servers.name: Context7 (Upstash)
servers.what: Looks up current documentation for software tools, so answers are not out of date.
servers.notes: Sends the name of the library you ask about to Upstash. Do not put private text in those questions. Works without a key at a lower rate limit [Unverified].

servers.name: Google Workspace (Taylor Wilsdon)
servers.what: Reads your Gmail, Google Calendar and Drive. Starts in read-only mode.
servers.notes: You create your own Google Cloud OAuth client (about five minutes, free). Remove --read-only only after you decide to allow drafts; the outbound guard sees this server under the channel other (it decides from the server name), so the default level, draft, blocks anything that sends. The email level in config/autonomy.json does not apply to it. See the google-workspace-local blueprint. The --read-only flag is in the README; the per-service permission names were not checked [Unverified].

servers.name: Canvas LMS (Vishal Sachdev)
servers.what: Reads your Canvas courses, deadlines, announcements and grades.
servers.notes: Needs a Canvas access token you create in your Canvas profile. Some schools switch tokens off or forbid automated access: check your school rules first. Some tools can post messages or submit work, and the outbound guard does not recognise this server as messaging (it decides from the server name), so the canvas-sync blueprint limits the sync skill to read-only tools. The command name canvas-mcp-server comes from the README install steps [Unverified until first run].

servers.name: Zotero (54yyyu)
servers.what: Searches your Zotero reading library and its notes.
servers.notes: Local mode talks to the Zotero desktop app, which must be open. No account keys needed in local mode [Unverified: confirm the ZOTERO_LOCAL variable on first run].

servers.name: QMD (Tobi Lutke)
servers.what: A fast search engine over your notes that finds meaning, not just exact words.
servers.notes: Downloads local AI models on first run (large). Windows support has had problems, for example with graphics-card settings, so test it before relying on it. Everything stays on your computer. The mcp sub-command is [Unverified]; confirm with qmd --help.

servers.name: Obsidian Local REST API (built-in MCP)
servers.what: Talks to Obsidian while it is open, for things like running commands and opening notes.
servers.notes: This is a plugin inside Obsidian, not a separate program. Endpoint: https://127.0.0.1:27124/mcp/ with an Authorization: Bearer header (or http://127.0.0.1:27123/mcp/ if you switch the plain HTTP option on). Needs Obsidian open. mcpvault is enough for most people.

servers.name: Firecrawl
servers.what: Reads hard websites (ones that need scripts to load) and returns clean text.
servers.notes: Sends the pages you ask for to the Firecrawl service. Watch your credit use. Put the key in .env.local, never in chat.

servers.name: Exa search
servers.what: A web search built for AI, good for finding companies, papers and people at work.
servers.notes: Your search words go to Exa. Do not include private details. The package name exa-mcp-server was verified on npm; a hosted option exists at https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp.

servers.name: Yahoo Finance (Alex2Yang97)
servers.what: Fetches share prices, company financials and news for case work.
servers.notes: Uses unofficial Yahoo data, which may break or be limited. For learning and case work only, never for trading decisions. Pinned to a commit because the repo has no release tags. Alterbrain gives no investment advice.

servers.name: Anki MCP (ankimcp)
servers.what: Creates and reviews flashcards in the Anki app.
servers.notes: Needs the Anki desktop app open with the AnkiConnect add-on. Alterbrain also has its own simple card system in the vault, so Anki is only for people who already use it. See the anki-fsrs blueprint.

servers.name: Microsoft 365 (Softeria)
servers.what: Reads your Outlook email, calendar and OneDrive files.
servers.notes: University and work Microsoft accounts often need an administrator to approve the app (tenant consent). Many schools say no. Check first. Read-only by default. The outbound guard sees this server under the channel other (it decides from the server name), so the default level, draft, blocks anything that sends. See the outlook-m365 blueprint.

servers.name: NotebookLM (PleasePrompto)
servers.what: Lets Alterbrain ask questions of your Google NotebookLM notebooks.
servers.notes: The repository was archived in September 2026 and is no longer maintained. It drives a browser logged in to your Google account, which Google may treat as a terms breach. Moved to avoid.

servers.name: LinkedIn (stickerdaniel)
servers.what: Reads LinkedIn profiles, companies and jobs by driving a real browser session.
servers.notes: LinkedIn forbids automated access, so your account could be limited or banned. It uses your own logged-in session. Read only a little, slowly, and never send messages or connection requests through it. The PyPI package is mcp-server-linkedin (the older name linkedin-scraper-mcp is an older release line). The --no-auto-import flag stops it copying a login from your everyday browser, so you sign in once on its own browser profile. On Windows, if the first sign-in stops with a PrivateStateError, create an empty folder inside your user folder (for example C:/Users/<you>/.linkedin-mcp-installer) and set the INSTALLER_TEMP_DIR environment variable to it, for the sign-in and for normal runs; the catalogue cannot fill in a per-user path for you. See the linkedin blueprint. For your own LinkedIn data without scraping, see the linkedin-data-portability blueprint.

servers.name: Instagram (official Graph API, no server)
servers.what: Posting to Instagram is only supported through Meta's official API, which needs a business account.
servers.notes: Blueprint-only entry: no server is recommended. Personal accounts cannot use the API for posting, and scraping tools break the rules [Unverified: check current Meta account rules]. See the instagram blueprint. Not selectable in mcp.selected.json.

servers.name: Telegram (chigwell)
servers.what: Lets Alterbrain read and send messages from your own Telegram account.
servers.notes: It acts as YOU on Telegram, using a session string that is as powerful as your login. Keep it in .env.local only. Never install it from PyPI: the README warns the telegram-mcp name there is a different package, so it is pinned to a git tag. For simple chat with Alterbrain use the official Telegram channel plugin instead (see the telegram-channel blueprint). Environment variable names are [Unverified]; confirm on first run.

servers.name: WhatsApp (lharries)
servers.what: Reads and sends WhatsApp messages by pretending to be a linked device.
servers.notes: No official personal WhatsApp API exists. This uses an unofficial route that can get your number banned, and it has had no update since July 2025. See the whatsapp-why-not blueprint.

servers.name: X / Twitter servers (various)
servers.what: Community servers that post to X.
servers.notes: The official API is paid and strict, and community servers vary a lot in quality. Not recommended. No specific server was checked.

servers.name: Browserbase
servers.what: A cloud browser service.
servers.notes: The repository is archived. Playwright does the same job locally.

servers.name: Office Word / PowerPoint servers (GongRzhe)
servers.what: Create Word and PowerPoint files.
servers.notes: Both repositories (Word and PowerPoint) are archived. Use Quarto for documents instead.
